ARTICLE III DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE; DESIGN GUIDELINES; DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE PROCEDURES 3.1 Construction/Alteration of Improvements. Per the Master Declaration and adopted Design Guidelines, construction of all Improvements on a Lot, and any alterations or modification of such Improvements (other than changes the interior thereof), must be approved, in writing, by the DRC. The submittal requirements and procedures for the DRC are set forth below. Except as expressly provided to the contrary in the Master Declaration or the Design Guidelines, no Improvement shall be constructed without the prior written consent of the DRC, and no changes or deviations in or from the plans and specifications consented to by the DRC shall be made without the prior written consent of the DRC. The approval rights of the DRC extend to aesthetic considerations as well as issues of design consistency and quality. 3.2 Design Guidelines. The Design Guidelines adopted for the Development consist of the Design Principles for Sterling Ranch and the appendices thereto, including, without limitation, the Water Demand Management Initiatives and the Technology Guidelines and Specifications. The Design Guidelines are subject to modification or amendment from time to time by the CAB. The terms and provisions of the Design Guidelines are incorporated herein by reference and made a part hereof as if set forth at length. OWNERS SHOULD REVIEW THE DESIGN GUIDELINES CAREFULLY. THE DESIGN GUIDELINES INCLUDE PROVISIONS RELATING TO DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION OF INTERIOR, EXTERIOR, LANDSCAPING AND IRRIGATION IMPROVEMENTS, AS WELL AS WATER BUDGETS OF THE LOTS. THE TIERED RATE STRUCTURE IN PLACE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT PROVIDES FOR INCREASED RATES FOR WATER CONSUMPTION BEYOND DEFINED VOLUMES. OUTDOOR WATER USE IN EXCESS OF THE WATER BUDGETS SET FORTH IN THE DESIGN GUIDELINES MAY RESULT IN SIGNIFICANT INCREASES IN UTILITY CHARGES. 3.3 Approval Request; Plans and Specifications. Each request for DRC approval (an “Approval Request”) at the conceptual design submittal and final design submittal phases described in Section 3.4 shall be accompanied by such plans and specifications of the proposed -- 6 of 21 -- {00440572} 7 Improvement as are set forth in the applicable Design Guidelines that show, to the extent applicable to the Improvement for which the approval is requested, the design and other characteristics thereof as are set forth in the applicable Design Guidelines and a review fee as established by the DRC (the “Review Fee”). The DRC will submit a schedule of proposed review fees annually to the CAB for review and approval. The DRC may postpone review of any material submitted until it has received all required or requested Plans and Specifications and other information. The DRC shall notify the Owner in writing upon receipt of all required Plans and Specifications and that the Owner’s Approval Request is complete. 3.4 Review Procedure. The DRC review process for Improvements generally consists of three stages: a pre-design meeting with the DRC, a conceptual design submittal and a mandatory final design submittal. While final design submittal is the only mandatory step, final design submittal applications made without prior completion of the pre-design meeting and conceptual design submittal have a significantly increased probability for denial by the DRC. Therefore, applicants are strongly encouraged to complete the pre-design meeting and the conceptual design submittal prior to submittal for final design approval, unless otherwise directed by the DRC. The DRC shall strive to approve, approve with conditions or deny a complete Approval Request within the later to occur of (a) 30 days after its receipt or (b) 10 days after the first meeting of the DRC following its receipt. The DRC’s failure to approve, approve with conditions or deny a complete Approval Request within such period shall be deemed a denial of such Approval Request. Approval of a majority of the members of the DRC, either at a meeting or in writing, shall be required to approve any Approval Request. If DRC approval is granted subject to conditions, the Owner shall revise its Plans and Specifications to incorporate such changes and shall deliver the required number of complete sets of revised Plans and Specifications (reflecting responses to all items) to the DRC, which shall again be reviewed in accordance with and in the timeframe described above. 3.5 Modifications to Approved Plans and Specifications. Any modification or change to an approved set of Plans and Specifications must again be submitted to the DRC for its approval in the same manner as for initial approval of Plans and Specifications. 3.6 Appeal of DRC Decision. If the DRC disapproves any part of the Plans and Specifications submitted (or approves the same subject to conditions), the Owner may, within ten (10) days after the DRC's disapproval or deemed disapproval, make a written request for a hearing before the CAB, or any appeals board established by the CAB in accordance with the Master Declaration, to reconsider the Plans and Specifications. A form of a request for a hearing for an Owner’s use is attached hereto as Exhibit E. If the Owner requires a hearing in accordance with the foregoing sentence, the hearing shall be held in executive session of the CAB or such appeals board, affording Owner a reasonable opportunity to be heard. The Owner shall be notified in writing of the decision within ten (10) days after the hearing. The decision of the CAB or the appeals board, as applicable, shall be final and binding upon the Owner. 3.7 Prosecution of Work; Notice of Completion; Notices of Noncompliance. All work approved by the DRC in an Approval Request must be diligently prosecuted to completion, and a Notice of Completion delivered to the DRC in connection therewith, in accordance with and within the time allotted in Article 3 of the Master Declaration. These water meters have been designed to be read remotely through the internet - as such, each home must have an internet connection for the meters to be read remotely. Any Owner replacing the Builder-installed water meter (other than with a CAB-approved water meter) or terminating the internet connection within his/her home must provide the CAB with written authorization to enter such home to manually read the water meter and pay the CAB a monthly or other fee established by the CAB from time to time in order to do so. Exceptions from the provisions of the Design Guidelines are considered by the DRC on a case-by-case basis for specific applications only, and shall not establish a precedent for any other project or future development. (a) Submittal Requirements for Technical Criteria Variance. (i) Criteria from which the variance is sought. (ii) Identification of the alternative design, improvement, construction technique or material proposed to be used. (iii) Supporting documentation including: justification for variance including how the intent of the criteria is still being achieved, related calculations, details, exhibits, etc. (iv) The variance request shall be signed by the owner or design professional. (b) Review Criteria for Technical Criteria Variances. A technical criteria variance may be approved if one or more of the following criteria are met, provided that no variance shall impose a detriment or injury to other property or improvements within the Property and will not militate against the general intent and purpose of the Design Guidelines and the Master Declaration: (i) The standards may be met by an alternative method that is demonstrated to have an equivalent or better function and meet the same objective. (ii) Physical constraints exist, such as steep topography or other natural hazards, which limit the ability to install the improvement, would limit healthy plant growth, or could cause safety concerns. -- 8 of 21 -- {00440572} 9 (iii) Site conditions, including geology, topography, indigenous soils, or issues related to water demand, may be better addressed through the alternative proposal. (iv) Any decision rendered by the CAB shall be final. ARTICLE IV ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE; ENFORCEMENT 4.1 Enforcement Committee. fullText: Adopted August 26, 2020 Adopted October 16, 2019 Water-Wise Tree Lawns at Providence Village A M STERLING RANCH COLORADO -- 1 of 18 -- Tree Lawns AN ESSENTIAL COMPONENT OF natural resource stewardship and responsible water management is specifying a significant portion of plant material that is native, naturalized, or adapted to the semi-arid high plains prairie ecosystem in which Providence Village is located. By incorporating the native or naturalized plantings of this geographic region in a way that meets the aesthetic character of the community, tree lawns in Providence Village can be a showcase of water demand management and a successful blending of nature and development. Tree lawns by deffinition refer to the landscape area between the sidewalk and street-curb. CuSTOMIzEd wATEr BudGETS have been predetermined for varying lot sizes in Providence Village. There is flexibility in using these water budgets to meet individual landscaping styles. For example, tree lawns planted with shrubs, grasses, and perennials and irrigated with a drip system will have a lower water demand than the same area planted entirely with turf and irrigated with a spray system. The water savings from the tree lawns can be applied towards additional planting elsewhere in the front yard or backyard landscape. ThE PLANT PALETTE provided on the following page is a recommended list of plant materials that use relatively little water, thrive in our sunny environment, and demonstrate the character of our community. This palette, along with the SAMPLE TREE LAWN PLANS provided, are being offered as a design tool to builders, designers, and homeowners who wish to substitute some turf in their tree lawns with a low water and relatively low maintenance alternative. While the species on this list are approved by Sterling Ranch, it is not exhaustive, and the landscape designer is responsible for following Douglas County requirements for plant height within sight visibility triangles for vehicles in the public right-of-way. -- 2 of 18 -- Shrubs Chamaebatiaria millefolium Caryopteris x clandonensis 'Dark Knight' Ericameria nauseosa var. speciosa Juniperus horizontalis Prunus besseyi 'Pawnee Buttes' Rhus trilobata 'Autumn Amber' Tree Lawn Palette Grasses Andropogon gerardii Bouteloua 'Blonde Ambition' Festuca 'Boulder Blue' Muhlenbergia 'Undaunted' Nassella tennuissima Panicum 'Heavy Metal' Panicum virgatum Sorghastrum nutans 'Indian Steel' Perennials Achillea 'Coronation Gold' Agastache cana Agastache 'Blue Fortune' Allium cernuum Aquilegia chrysantha Artemisia 'French' Asclepias incarnata 'Cinderella' Aster 'Lady in Black' Baptisia austalis Crambe maritima Centranthus rubur Coreopsis verticillata 'Moonbeam' Delosperma cooperi Echinacea pallida Echinacea paradoxa Echinacea purpurea Echinacea tennessensis Eupatorium 'Gateway' Fragraria 'Ft. fullText: RESOLUTION NO. 2023-04-02 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY AUTHORITY BOARD MODIFYING THE CODE RULES OF THE STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY AUTHORITY BOARD (Artificial Turf, Technology Guidelines, Table 13-23) RECITALS A. WHEREAS, the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (the "CAB") is an authority and separate legal entity created pursuant to section 29-1-203, C.R.S., and in conformity with section 29-1-203.5, C.R.S., and that certain Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Establishment Agreement, (the "CABEA"), by and between the Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan District Nos. 1-7 (collectively, the "Sterling Ranch Districts"); and B. WHEREAS, pursuant to the CABEA, the CAB Board (the “Board”) shall govern the business and affairs of the CAB and establish the policies, rules and regulations of the CAB; and C. WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 32-1-1001(m), C.R.S., CAB has the authority to adopt, amend and enforce rules and regulations for the carrying on of business and to meet the objectives of the CAB; and D. WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 32-1-1001(j), C.R.S., the CAB has the authority to adopt and from time to time increase or decrease fees, rates, tolls, penalties, or charges for services, programs or facilities E. WHEREAS, the CAB has adopted the Code of Rules of the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board which contains the rules, regulations, fees, charges, rates, tolls and penalties set forth by the CAB; and F. WHEREAS, the CAB has reviewed the rules and regulations related to front and rear yard landscape requirements to provide for sustainable, water conscious, and drought tolerant options; and G. WHEREAS, the CAB has determined certain updates to the fees, rates, charges, tolls and penalties charged for certain design review activities should be updated; and H. WHEREAS, the CAB has determined to update its rule regarding certain Technology Guidelines to reflect certain changes and specifications from technology providers; and I. WHEREAS, the Board has determined that modification to certain rules and regulations should be modified, and is in the best interest of the CAB and its residents to do so. DocuSign Envelope ID: 9EF31321-95DF-46BE-9E03-A183087CD19B -- 1 of 14 -- NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY AUTHORITY BOARD OF THE COUNTY OF DOUGLAS, COLORADO: 1. The following rules and regulations are hereby modified as described on the attached Exhibit A. 2. The Board directs that these changes be incorporated into the published version of the Code of Rules and Regulations of the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (the “Code”) when that document is next updated or supplemented. Any reference to a section of the Rules and Regulations herein shall be considered a reference to the corresponding section of the Code. ADOPTED AND APPROVED this 19th day of April, 2023. STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY AUTHORITY BOARD By: President Attest: Secretary/Assistant Secretary DocuSign Envelope ID: 9EF31321-95DF-46BE-9E03-A183087CD19B -- 2 of 14 -- Exhibit A Amended Artificial Turf Guidelines The following provisions of the Code of Rules of the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board are hereby amended to read as follows: Sec. 9-176. - Required landscape materials. Approved Language (c) Artificial turf will be considered for the front and/or the rear yard on a case-by-case basis. Specific guidelines for artificial turf installation are provided in Section 21-22. Sec. 5-151. - Required lot landscape. Approved Language (a) Artificial turf will be evaluated on an individual basis for front yards. (b) The front yard shall consist of a combination of trees, sodded turf, and shrubs. Perennial and groundcover beds are not required, but are strongly encouraged to provide variety and personalization to the home. Annual plantings may also be part of the overall design. Chapter 21 - Structures and Uses; Article II. - Residential Standards; Sec. 21-22. - General community standards Approved Language - Currently no language that addresses artificial turf; need to add proposed language as a new category in alphabetical order as No. 7 (all other numbers should shift down accordingly). 7) Artificial turf. All installations require DRC approval and will be considered on a case-by-case basis. a. The DRC will evaluate the use of artificial turf in the landscape design and consider the square footage of artificial turf in combination with the square footage of live coverage. b. Submissions must include the following materials and information: 1. Plot plan with location of turf including distances to property lines, easements, sidewalk, driveway and drainage ways, square footage of turf installation and percentage of artificial turf coverage in yard.2. Product specification sheet that includes details on color, materials, pile height, face weight of backing and infill requirements.3. Product specifications for all aggregate base materials, infill materials, seaming materials and adhesives. 4. Copy of manufacturer’s warranty for all materials, workmanship, and installers warranty statement for workmanship for construction for a minimum of 1 year workmanship warranty.5. Detailed product photos are required and DRC reserves the right to request a 12-inch by 12-inch sample of the exact artificial turf if photos are not clear. c. Please note that all installations must appear natural at all times. d. Any deviation from a natural look due to improper installation or lack of maintenance will be in violation of these rules and require repair or removal. DocuSign Envelope ID: 9EF31321-95DF-46BE-9E03-A183087CD19B -- 3 of 14 -- e. As Colorado water laws and product market availability change over time, DRC reserves the right to revisit guidelines. f. Product improvements may occur at any time. The Design Review Committee reserves the right to review new products and solutions as they become available and may modify the artificial turf specifications and guidelines as needed. g. Artificial turf is not allowed in tree lawns. h. Turf may not contain lead or PFAS chemicals i. Specialized surfaces for putting greens, play areas, bocce ball and other uses are allowed in rear yards only. j. Artificial turf may not be placed in drainage swells or near discharge from sump pumps. k. Antibacterial infill required for areas intended for pet use. Silica sand allowed in non-pet areas. l. 6-inches of compacted native soil topped with weed barrier is required. m. A minimum of a 4-inch sub-base aggregate on top of the weed barrier and compacted to 95% is additionally required. n. For the sub-base aggregate, 2-inches of larger aggregate topped with 2-inches of compacted breeze is preferred for optimal drainage. o. Infill per square foot should be a minimum 2lbs per square foot, worked ½ way into depth of turf. p. Seam tape and glue is required on all seams. Seams may not be readily visible. q. Front Yard Installations 1. Artificial turf cannot exceed 30% percent of the square footage of the front yard and the front yard must still include a combination of grasses, shrubs, perennials, annuals, and required trees. 2. Artificial turf must be interior to the lot and buffered with live plant material. 3. Live plant material must be included between house foundation and turf. 4. Turf pile is required to have color variation (field green/olive, green/clover, green/tan, field green/apple, etc.). 5. Pile height must be a minimum 1.75-inches. 6. Face weight (density of the fibers on top of the backing) must be a minimum 60-ounce. 7. Artificial turf backing required to have minimum hole punches every 4-inches for drainage, completely perforated backing preferred. 8. Required to have an element of “thatch” and needs to be brown or beige, or tan, or a color that is different from the turf piles. 9. Artificial turf is required to be a minimum of 5-feet from side property lines, 3-feet from back of sidewalk and may not be installed over trench drains. 10. Turf must be installed so that the tips of the piles face toward the primary street frontage of the lot. DocuSign Envelope ID: 9EF31321-95DF-46BE-9E03-A183087CD19B -- 4 of 14 -- 11. 15-foot maximum width preferred to reduce seams. 12. Fix turf down around the perimeter with edging, bend-a-board or similar product. Secure a minimum of every 6-inches with 5-inch or 6-inch nongalvanized nails or turf staples - recommend every 4- inches at edges adjacent to concrete to avoid lift at edges and tripping hazard. r. Rear Yard Installations 1. Artificial turf cannot exceed 30% percent of the square footage of the rear yard and the rear yard must still include a combination of grasses, shrubs, perennials, annuals, and required trees. 2. Artificial turf must be interior to the lot and buffered with live plant material to ensure adequate visual screening toward community. 3. Turf pile is required to have color variation (field green/olive, green/clover, green/tan, field green/apple, etc.) 4. Artificial turf backing required to have minimum hole punches every 4-inches for drainage, completely perforated backing preferred. 5. Required to have an element of “thatch” and needs to be brown or beige, or tan, or a color that is different from the turf piles unless turf is specialized surface for putting greens, bocce ball and other similar type uses. 6. Artificial turf is required to be a minimum of 5-feet from side and rear property lines. s. Artificial Turf Maintenance 1. Artificial turf will fade over time. Faded turf will require replacement. Color fade between older product and replacement product may not be visible. 2. Power broom maintenance is required when artificial turf becomes matted. Recommend power broom and power wash once a year to stand fibers up and deep clean product. fullText: 9350 Roxborough Park Road, Sterling Ranch, Colorado 80125 Re: Fire Risk Management March 28, 2025 To whom it may concern, As part of our commitment to safety and risk management, I would like to outline the fire risk mitigation practices followed by the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (SRCAB). Our community adheres to Douglas County’s Wildfire Mitigation Standards, and we have also implemented additional measures specific to our locale. As a result, our community has an ISO Class 1 (or PPC1) fire protection rating, which is the highest level of fire protection a community can achieve. Sensible Landscape Design: o We prioritize landscape designs that minimize fire risk adjacent to developed areas. This includes limiting certain types of grasses, shrubs, and trees. By carefully planning our green spaces, we create a buffer zone that reduces the likelihood of fire spreading to inhabited areas. Vegetation Management: o Adjacent to developed areas, we employ several practices to maintain vegetation health and prevent overgrowth. These practices include: § Mow Strips: Along single-family lots, trails, and roadways, we establish mow strips. These cleared areas act as firebreaks, reducing the risk of flames reaching structures. § Regular Inspections: Our team inspects vegetation health regularly. Prompt action is taken if any hazardous conditions are identified. Emergency Access and Fire Breaks: o The proposed and existing regional trail network serves dual purposes: emergency access routes and fire breaks. These designated trails allow swift response during emergencies and create natural firebreaks. Livestock Grazing: o In existing undeveloped open spaces, controlled livestock grazing helps manage vegetation. Grazing reduces fuel loads and maintains defensible spaces. Collaboration with Heavy Equipment Operators: o As a developing community, we have established arrangements with heavy equipment operators. In the event of wildfire, they can assist in creating fire stops by clearing vegetation and creating defensible zones. Having heavy equipment accessible reduces response times. -- 1 of 2 -- Appropriate Building Materials: o When constructing fences in developed areas, we select materials that do not increase fire risk. Fire-resistant materials are preferred to enhance safety. o For structures and exterior decks, we choose materials that minimize fire risk. Our guidelines ensure that construction materials meet safety standards and do not contribute to fire propagation. South Metro Fire Rescue: o Sterling Ranch is rated ISO1 with South Metro Fire Rescue. o Sterling Ranch is served by South Metro Fire Rescue (SMFR). SMFR has two stations within minutes of the community. Station 40 is located near Titan Parkway and U.S. Highway 85 and has equipment specially designed for urban interface fires. Station 19 is located near Trailmark Parkway and S. Wadsworth Boulevard and has a wildland apparatus. Douglas County Wildfire Action Collaborative (DCWAC): o Aerial support for wildfires is provided through the County’s contract with Trans Aero LTD and now provides for use of a Type 2 helicopter capable of delivering 300 gallons of water to the front lines of a wildfire any time an elevate fire danger warrants activation. This helicopter is stationed on the east side of Sterling Ranch. We remain committed to safeguarding our residents and property. If you have any further inquiries or require additional documentation, please feel free to email us at info@SterlingRanchCAB.com or call (720) 661-9694. Sincerely, Jessica Gottschalk Director of Community Experience and Resident Support Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board -- 2 of 2 --

fullText: RESOLUTION NO. 2024-05-04 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY AUTHORITY BOARD AMENDING THE CODE OF RULES OF THE STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY AUTHORITY BOARD RECITALS A. WHEREAS, the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (the "CAB") is an authority and separate legal entity created pursuant to section 29-1-203, C.R.S., and in conformity with section 29-1-203.5, C.R.S., and that certain Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Establishment Agreement, (the "CABEA"), by and between the Sterling Ranch Colorado Metropolitan District Nos. 1-7 (collectively, the "Sterling Ranch Districts"); and B. WHEREAS, pursuant to the CABEA, the CAB Board (the “Board”) shall govern the business and affairs of the CAB and establish the policies, rules and regulations of the CAB; and C. WHEREAS, all capitalized terms used herein shall have the same meaning as used in the Master Declaration of Covenants Conditions and Restrictions for Sterling Ranch Planned Development recorded September 28, 2015 with the Douglas County Clerk and Recorder at Reception No. 2015069869 (“Master Declaration”) unless otherwise defined herein; and D. WHEREAS, pursuant to Sections 2.1 and 2.2. of the Master Declaration CAB was delegated, and accepted on behalf of the District’s, governance and enforcement powers of the Documents in the Sterling Ranch community; and E. WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 2.3 of the Master Declaration, the CAB has the authority to adopt rules and regulations implementing the Declaration and has adopted the Code of Rules of the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (the “CAB Code”); and F. WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 32-1-1001(m), C.R.S., CAB has the authority to adopt, amend and enforce rules and regulations for the carrying on of business and to meet the objectives of the CAB; and G. Richard Shaw III, Assistant Secretary DocuSign Envelope ID: D1150142-89CE-4A36-A9A0-183EBF611081 -- 2 of 8 -- Exhibit A Amendments to CAB Code Rule Adopted Language Section 21-22 (b) See below. (56) Lighting. a. General. DRC approval is required to modify or add exterior lighting. This includes, but is not limited to, motion detector spotlights, security lighting, landscape lighting, architectural accent lighting, decorative lighting, ballasted fixtures, additional lighting at doors or windows, etc. "Cut sheets" (product description, specifications and illustrations) must be submitted to the Design Review Committee for each type of fixture proposed for review. 1. All exterior lighting must be compliant with these Rules and Douglas County's "Dark Skies" guidelines (https://www.douglas.co.us/planning/developmentreview-regulations/developmentinfo-assistance/development-outdoor-lighting/). To minimize the effects of light pollution, lighting should: . Only be on when needed; . Only light the area that needs it; . Be no brighter than necessary . Be used only when needed; . Use warmer color lights where possible. 2. Exterior Lighting Replacement Program: To replace exterior light fixtures on your home, follow the “Five Lighting Principles for Responsible Outdoor Lighting” guidelines in 21-22(b)(56)(a)(1), select a fixture where the bulb is fully shielded with the cone of light pointing down to minimize skyglow, glare and light trespass, and submit an Exterior Lighting Improvement application. 3. Lighting techniques that "up light" buildings or landscape (trees, shrubs, etc.) and shine light into the sky shall not be permitted. 4. Exterior light fixtures must be fully shielded so that the lamp bulb or LED cluster is not visible from property lines or the street, have a warm white light with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700 Kelvin is preferred). DocuSign Envelope ID: D1150142-89CE-4A36-A9A0-183EBF611081 -- 3 of 8 -- 5. Exterior lighting must be directed downward, so that the light cone does not cause glare to adjacent properties or on to the street. 6. At any time, unduly bright lights that create a nuisance to adjacent owners or lighting complaints received may be re-evaluated. 7. Utilizing photocell and timers to control switching of site lighting is highly encouraged. 8. Exterior lighting that lights an outdoor living space (such as a patio, porch, or deck) shall light only the livable space and not extend beyond that area. b. Under-eave lighting. This type of lighting provides an architectural accent to homes and businesses. Canned lighting installed into front porch soffits/ceilings is included in this section. Architectural accent lighting includes appropriately spaced, recessed lighting strategically placed to enhance DocuSign Envelope ID: D1150142-89CE-4A36-A9A0-183EBF611081 -- 4 of 8 -- architectural elements such as columns. Architectural accent lighting shall not flash, change colors, etc. 1. Lighting must consist of hardwired fixtures installed into the soffit or hardwired track eave/rake lighting systems such as Jellyfish or Gemstone. 2. Gemstone and Jellyfish systems are the approved systems. Other similar companies/products are not permitted. a. Other companies can apply to be added to the approved list of dark sky-compliant lighting systems if they meet the following standards: . Match house trim . Downward facing . Limited cone of light . As hidden as possible . Hardwired . Functionality to include architectural lighting options. 3. Under-eave lighting may be installed on the front of the home using logical termination points from the front to the sides. Elevations showing termination points must be submitted with the application. Termination points may not extend further than the wing fence. 4. Under-eave lighting may be installed on the rear of the home if it backs up to open space, subject to DRC approval, and will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. 5. Corner lots can install under-eave lighting on the side of the home that abuts the street, subject to DRC approval, which will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. 6. Under-eave lighting shall not be used as security lighting. For security lighting rules, please see section f. 7. Hardwired canned lighting installed into the soffit/ceiling of the front porch shall light only the front porch and not extend beyond that area. 8. Under-eave hardwired track eave/rake lighting systems or hardwired canned lighting can be installed under a roofed cover above a rear deck or rear patio, subject to DRC approval, which will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. a. Light cone does not cause glare to adjacent properties or onto the street; and b. It is a warm light, with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700 Kelvin preferred). 9. Lighting must be warm white with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700 Kelvin is preferred). 10. Architectural style may restrict some uses. 11. During non-holiday lighting periods, lighting must adhere to the following rules: a. Lighting must be warm white with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700 Kelvin is preferred). b. At no time shall the lights be programmed to strobe, flash, pulse, chase or have any pattern outside of approved architectural accent lighting as defined below. They must remain static. 12. A homeowner may install traditional under-eave lighting, or use track lighting systems in a static pattern to accent the home architecturally. a. Architectural accent lighting is where lights are spaced to enhance architectural elements such as columns, building corners and gable peaks; or 12. All under-eave lighting must be turned off by 10:00 p.m. PHOTOS OF ACCEPTABLE AND NOT ACCEPTABLE LIGHTING PATTERNS WILL BE INCLUDED. This type of lighting is installed to provide low-level lighting to create ambiance for rear outside use areas. 1. Lighting must consist of café, globe, or lit rope style lights. LED string lights/cords, "holiday decoration style" string lights, and other forms of lighting are not allowed. 2. Lighting must be strung under or on structural elements such as pergolas, gazebos, decks/patio covers or comparable structural items in the rear yard with a limited number of lights so as not to over light the area or impact surrounding property owners. 3. Low-level decorative lighting cannot cause glare to adjacent properties. 4. Must be a warm white light, with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700 Kelvin preferred). 5. Light cone does not cause glare to adjacent properties or onto the street; and iii. It is a warm white light, with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700 Kelvin preferred). 6. All outdoor decorative lighting must be turned off by 10:00 p.m. d. Landscape lighting. This type of lighting is intended to provide low-level illumination at ground level to landscaping features, sidewalks or other similar low improvements. 1. Landscape should only be used to provide such as walking paths, retaining walls, steps, etc. All landscape lights should be kept to a minimum. 2. Up-lighting is not an approved Dark Sky lighting type and is not permitted. Lights must have a downward facing cone of light. 3. Lighting must be warm white with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less (2,700 Kelvin is preferred). Colored lighting is not allowed. 4. Solar in-ground lighting is permitted in front and rear yards without DRC approval provided that: i. No light fixture shall exceed 36 inches in height. ii. Placement of fixtures is limited to edges of walks, driveways, and planting beds. iii. The light "cone" is downward facing and does not cause glare onto surrounding properties or the street. iv. No more than eight such fixtures shall be permitted in the front yard. 5. In the rear transition zone, solar in-ground down lighting provided that it is less than 36 inches in height, is placed along edges of walks or planting beds and cone of light is downward facing not causing glare off of property is allowed. See Section 9-233 for additional transition zone guidelines. DocuSign Envelope ID: D1150142-89CE-4A36-A9A0-183EBF611081 -- 6 of 8 -- 6. All landscape lighting, with the exception of solar in-ground lighting, must be turned off by 10:00 p.m. e. Seasonal decorative lighting. Seasonal decorative lighting may include hardwired traditional soffit installed lighting, hardwired track eave/rake lighting or temporary string lighting installed for the approved seasonal period. 1. Seasonal decorative lighting should be installed or operated in a manner that does not create any light trespass beyond the property boundaries or glare onto surrounding properties. 2. If using temporary string lighting, use low wattage string lights, LED preferred. 3. Seasonal decorative lighting may be of various colors and patterns and is permitted to blink, flash, chase, or strobe. DocuSign Envelope ID: D1150142-89CE-4A36-A9A0-183EBF611081 -- 7 of 8 -- 4. Install and energize seasonal decorative lighting during the following approved seasonal lighting periods: From June 18 to July 7 and from October 1 through January 31. Outside of these approved seasonal lighting periods all temporary string lighting and light installation clips are required to be removed, and all hardwired traditional soffit installed lighting and hardwired track eave/rake lighting must be returned to the settings allowed in Section b. above. 5. At the sole discretion of the CAB, removal dates for seasonal decorative lighting may be extended due to extreme weather conditions or other factors. During this time lighting may not be energized. 6. All holiday lighting must be turned off by 10:00 p.m. f. Security Lighting. This type of lighting is installed for area lighting for security purposes. It includes wall-mounted fixture lighting, as well as floodlights and spotlights to illuminate portions of the lot for security purposes. 1. Security lighting must be directed at the ground and house. 2. The light cone must stay within the property boundaries. 3. The light source shall not cause glare to other properties. 4. Lighting, except for that on the front of the home and facing the public street, shall conform to the following guidelines: i. Lights cannot be on 24/7. ii. Lights must be on photocell control and motion activated. Once activated by motion, the lighting setting must be adjusted so it cannot stay on longer than five minutes. 5. Spotlights, floodlights, or other similar lights used for security applications may only be used on front porches, over garage doors, or over rear porches/decks. 6. Security Lighting may be installed on the rear of the home if it backs up to an open space. Lighting will not be permitted in the rear if the open space is a designated wildlife corridor. DocuSign Envelope ID: D1150142-89CE-4A36-A9A0-183EBF611081 -- 8 of 8 --

fullText: RESOLUTION 2024-11-04 STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY AUTHORITY BOARD POLICY REGARDING DISPUTE RESOLUTION Adopted November 22, 2024 The following procedures have been adopted by Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (“CAB”) pursuant to the provisions of C.R.S. 32-1-1004.5(5) at a regular meeting of the Board of Directors. Purpose: To provide a more efficient means of resolving disputes or claims involving either the CAB and/or the CABs’ governing documents and to reduce the costs and fees associated with dispute resolution. WHEREAS, the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board is a public corporation formed, in part, to provide covenant enforcement and design review services pursuant to the Master Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Sterling Ranch Planned Development, recorded on September 28, 2015 at Reception No. 2015069869 in the real property records of Douglas County, Colorado and the Service Plans of the Metropolitan Districts with jurisdiction over the properties subject to said Master Declaration; and Whereas, pursuant to the authority delegated to CAB by the Master Declaration, and as provided under §32-1-1001, C.R.S., CAB has adopted a Code of Rules for the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (the “Code”); and WHEREAS, the CAB desires to provide clarity and specificity regarding its dispute resolution procedures. NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED that the CAB does hereby adopt the following policy governing the resolution of disputes: 1. Dispute Resolution Procedures. The CAB and Owners shall each follow the dispute resolution procedures set forth in Article 10 of the Master Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Sterling Ranch Planned Development, recorded on September 28, 2015 at Reception No. 2015069869 in the real property records of Douglas County, Colorado, and as further set forth in the Code. fullText: RESOLUTION 2024-11-03 STERLING RANCH COMMUNITY AUTHORITY BOARD POLICY GOVERNING DUE PROCESS AND IMPOSITION OF FINES Adopted November 22, 2024 The following Policy has been adopted by the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board pursuant to the provisions of C.R.S. 32-1-1004.5(2) by the Board of Directors. WHEREAS, the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (“CAB”) is a public corporation formed, in part, to provide covenant enforcement and design review services pursuant to the Service Plans for the Metropolitan Districts that encumber properties within Sterling Ranch; and WHEREAS, the CAB desires to set forth uniform processes and procedures governing the imposition of fines for violations of the covenants and rules that govern properties within Sterling Ranch (the “Documents”), and to ensure due process for all parties that may be subject to fines. NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED that the CAB does hereby adopt the following policies and procedures for the enforcement of the restrictive covenants and rules applicable to properties within Sterling Ranch, and the imposition of fines: 1. Power. The Board of Directors shall have the power and duty to hear and make decisions regarding violations and complaints filed with the Board and impose fines or other sanctions, pursuant to this policy. The Board may determine enforcement action on a case by case basis, and take other actions as it may deem necessary and appropriate to assure compliance with the Master Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Sterling Ranch Planned Development, recorded on September 28, 2015 at Reception No. 2015069869 in the real property records of Douglas County, Colorado (“Covenants”), the Code of Rules of the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board adopted by the Board and as amended from time to time (the “Code”),the Service Plans adopted by Metropolitan Districts with jurisdiction over properties in Sterling Ranch, applicable resolutions, and rules and regulations (collectively the “Documents”) promulgated thereunder, and to create a safe and harmonious living environment. Pursuant to the provisions set forth in the Master Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Sterling Ranch Planned Development, recorded on September 28, 2015 at Reception No. 2015069869 in the real property records of Douglas County, Colorado (“Covenants”) the Board has the authority to create an “Enforcement Committee” to be responsible for the ministerial administration and enforcement of the Documents. On May 20, 2020, the Board adopted Resolution No. 2020-05-04 Adopting a Policy Concerning the Formation and Function of Committees, and on June 17, 2020, the Board adopted Resolution No. 2020-06-03 Creating an Enforcement Committee. On February 17, 2021 the Board adopted Resolution No. 2021-02-01, an Amended and Restated Resolution of the Board of Directors the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Adopting a Policy Concerning the Formation and Function of Committees (the “Committee Resolution”). The Board has determined to rename -- 1 of 6 -- the Enforcement Committee the Community Standards Committee (the “CS Committee”) for the purposes carrying out the ministerial and administrative acts, to enforce the Documents and exercise the duties and obligations of the “Enforcement Committee” as provided in the Documents in the best interests of the CAB, the Districts, and the community as a whole. These enforcement provisions may be in addition to other specific provisions outlined in the Documents, and the CAB is not required to follow these enforcement provisions before seeking such other remedies. The CAB may choose a legal remedy or seek assistance from other enforcement authorities, such as police, fire, or animal control, as it deems appropriate. 2. Complaint. A proceeding to determine if the Documents have been violated and any enforcement measures and remedies that may apply may be initiated by the filing of a complaint with or by the CAB’s CS Committee, or as a result of an inspection performed by the CAB’s staff. If not readily apparent, the complaint shall state the specific provision(s) of the Documents alleged to have been violated and as many specifics as are available as to time, date, location and persons involved. To the extent possible, pictures shall accompany any written complaint. 3. Notice of Complaint and Warning Letter. Upon receipt of a complaint by a party other than the CAB’s staff, if the CS Committee determines that the allegations in the complaint are sufficient to constitute a violation of the Documents and that action is warranted, the CS Committee shall send a warning letter (“Warning Letter”) to the person(s) (the “Respondent”) alleged to have violated the Documents, by prepaid, first class United States mail addressed to the mailing address of the Respondent appearing on the records of the CAB or by electronic mail at an address which has been provided to the CAB by the Owner/Respondent or which the CAB has previously used for routine communications with the Owner/Respondent. If the alleged violation is observed as a result of an inspection performed by the CAB’s staff, the staff may send the Warning Letter without additional CS Committee approval. The Warning Letter shall advise the Respondent of the following: (1) the details of the complaint, or include a copy of the complaint; (2) that the CAB has reason to believe that the Respondent has violated the covenants or rules of the CAB; and (3) directing that the Respondent take specific action within a specified period of time from the date of the Warning Letter to come into compliance, or that further enforcement action will be taken, which may include the imposition of fines. 4. Continuous and Repetitious Violations; Nuisance Violations. A “Continuous Violation” is a violation that continues without abatement (such as painting a home without prior approval). A “Repetitious Violation” is a violation that may occur intermittently (such as a failure to remove weeds from the property, or a failure to retrieve trash cans in a timely manner). A “Nuisance Violation” means violations as specified in the Code. 5. Continued or Repeated Violation; Notice of Violation. If the CAB determines, not later than ten days after the date of the Warning Letter or such other date as is specified in the Warning Letter, that either the violation has not been cured or that it is a Repetitious Violation that has recurred within six months of the Warning Letter, the CAB shall send a Notice of Violation to the Respondent, by prepaid, first class United States mail addressed to the mailing address of the Respondent appearing on the records of the CAB or by electronic mail at an -- 2 of 6 -- address which has been provided to the CAB by the Owner/Respondent or which the CAB has previously used for routine communications with the Owner/Respondent. The Notice of Violation shall advise the Respondent of the following: (1) the details of the Continuous or Repetitious Violation; (2) the action the Respondent must take to cure the violation; (3) the action that may be taken if the violation is not cured, including fines imposed pursuant to this policy; (4) the Respondent’s right to be heard, either orally or in writing, by the CS Committee which is at least fifteen (15) days after the date of the notice; (5) the process by which to request a hearing; and (6) the CS Committee’s right to proceed with or without a hearing, at its discretion, to make its determination of the allegations based on all relevant facts and circumstances, if the Respondent fails to request a hearing, appear at the specified date and time, or otherwise respond to the Notice of Violation. 6. Hearing. Each hearing shall be held at the scheduled time, place and date, unless the Respondent has failed to respond or appear at the hearing. The CS Committee may grant continuances for good cause. Each hearing shall be held by the CS Committee which shall be an impartial decision-maker. The CS Committee is appointed by the Board and comprised of individuals who do not have any direct personal or financial interest in the outcome of the hearing. A person is deemed not to have a direct personal or financial interest if he/she will not receive any greater benefit or detriment from the outcome than will the other property owners within the community. The CS Committee may: (a) exercise its discretion as to the specific manner in which a hearing shall be conducted; (b) question witnesses and review evidence; and (c) act as it may deem appropriate or desirable to permit it to reach a just decision. Neither the complainant nor the Respondent must be in attendance at the hearing, but both are encouraged to attend. Any party may elect not to present evidence at the hearing. Any decision by the CS Committee shall be fair and reasonable taking into consideration all of the relevant facts and circumstances. Each hearing shall be open to the public. The CS Committee may convene a Hearing Panel comprised of no more than two (2) CS Committee members and the CS Committee CAB staff liaison for the purpose of hearing sensitive information related to a hearing. The Hearing Panel shall report back to the CS Committee during the formal hearing. 7. Decision. If the Respondent does not appear but a written response is filed, the CS Committee shall render its decision based on the information contained in the Complaint and the written response, considering all of the relevant facts and circumstances. If neither an appearance nor a written response is made, the CS Committee need not conduct a hearing or make any further findings except that it may determine that the Respondent’s failure to appear or respond constitutes a waiver of the right to a hearing, and a no contest plea to the alleged violation, and impose the sanctions provided for herein. If an appearance is made, after all testimony and other evidence has been presented to the CS Committee at a hearing, the CS Committee shall render its decision(s), taking into consideration all of the relevant facts and circumstances. The CS Committee decision shall be made in writing and transmitted to the Respondent within 10 days as provided in the Code. A Respondent may appeal a decision of the CS Committee to the full Board by following the procedure set forth in the Code. 8. Enforcement. The provisions of this policy shall not limit, or be a condition precedent to, the CAB’s right to enforce the Documents by any means available to the CAB, including, but not limited to, commencement of a lawsuit to force compliance or seeking -- 3 of 6 -- injunctive relief or damages. The CAB shall be entitled to reimbursement of all reasonable attorney’s fees and costs incurred by the CAB in connection with any enforcement action, including any proceeding under this policy. Without limiting the CAB’s remedies under the Documents, the Hearing Committee may assess fines, suspend Ownership privileges, and impose other sanctions in accordance with this policy. If the violation involves damage to CAB property, the violator shall also pay the costs of repair or replacement. The Hearing Committee may revoke or suspend the violator’s privileges for a period of time equal to the duration of the violation and for up to sixty (60) days thereafter, unless such violation is a continuing violation, in which case such suspension may continue for so long as such violation continues and for up to sixty (60) days thereafter. 9. Fines. Fines may be levied by the CS Committee for violations of the Documents as follows: Continuous Violations Fine Amount Warning Letter $0.00 First Notice of Violation (30 days to correct) $100.00 Second Notice of Violation (14 days to correct) $250.00 Third Notice of Violation (14 days to correct) $500.00 Continuing Violation $10.00 per day until cured Repetitious Violations Warning Letter $0.00 First Notice of Violation (30 days to correct) $100.00 Second Notice of Violation (14 days to correct) $250.00 Third Notice of Violation (14 days to correct) $500.00 Continuing Violation $10.00 per day until cured Nuisance Violations Warning Letter $0.00 First Notice of Violation (30 days to correct) $25.00 Second Notice of Violation (14 days to correct) $50.00 Third Notice of Violation (14 days to correct) $100.00 Continuing Violation $10.00 per day until cured 10. Responsibility for Actions of Tenant or Guest. Owners shall at all times be responsible for the actions of their tenants and guests. In the event that an Owner’s tenant or guest violates the Documents and a fine is imposed, the fine shall be assessed against that Owner. 11. Violations or Offenses that Constitute a Present Danger. If, in its sole discretion, the Board deems that any alleged violation is or may be an immediate or substantial threat to the health, safety or welfare of the community or an individual, the Board may take the appropriate action necessary to abate the threat to health, safety or welfare of the community or individual. -- 4 of 6 -- 12. Deviations. The Board may deviate from the procedures set forth in this policy if in its sole discretion such deviation is reasonable under the circumstances, except that fines shall not be levied unless the Board reasonably believes Respondent has received in some form notice of the opportunity for a hearing prior to fine(s) being levied. 13. Miscellaneous. 13.1 Failure by the CAB to enforce any provision of this policy shall in no event be deemed to be a waiver of the right to do so thereafter. 13.2 Fines imposed pursuant to this policy shall become a lien imposed against the record Owner’s real estate and enforceable as provided in the Covenants; provided that the CAB shall not foreclose on any lien that arises from amounts that an Owner owes the CAB as a result of a covenant violation or enforcement of a failure to comply with any Document. The Board, by resolution and at a public meeting held after notice has been provided to the affected Owner, may elect to have certain delinquent fees, rates, tolls, fines, penalties, charges, or assessments made or levied for covenant enforcement and design review services certified to the Treasurer of Douglas County, and for the delinquent fees, rates, tolls, fines, penalties, charges, or assessments to be collected and paid over by the Treasurer in the same manner as taxes are authorized to be collected and paid over pursuant to section 39-10-107. 13.3 The provisions of this policy shall be independent and severable. The invalidity of any one or more of the provisions hereof by judgment or court order or decree shall in no way affect the validity or enforceability of any of the other provisions, which other provisions shall remain in full force and effect. 13.4 Amendment of the Code shall be an administrative amendment to this Resolution. 13.5 The CAB, without needing to commence a legal proceeding, may seek reimbursement for collection costs and reasonable attorney fees incurred as a result of the Owner’s failure to comply. In any civil action to enforce or defend the CAB’s Documents, the court shall award reasonable attorney fees, costs, and costs of collection to the prevailing party. This is to verify amendments have been incorporated into the soil in the quantity specified and to the depth required. Per the Water Demand Management Initiatives, the specification is 4 cubic yards of soil amendment for each 1000 square feet, tilled to a depth of 6 inches. Soil Amendment must be a combination of aged ground manure and compost. fullText: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Design Review 13 All Content How do I get the Sterling Ranch Rules and Regulations documents? The best way to make sure you are using the most up-to-date version of Sterling Ranch rules and regulations is to download any needed documents at the link below. Design Review Documents Design Review Why do we need processes and guidelines to maintain architectural and community standards? We need a basis for treating all homeowners fairly and reasonably. Written guidelines allow homeowners and the Design Review Committee to work from the same criteria. Sometimes architectural requirements can be complex. The guidelines show exactly what is required and help design improvements that comply with the Community’s standards. Design Review What is required for the rear yard at initial installation? In the rear-yard one deciduous tree (minimum 1-1/2" caliper, measured 6 inches above ground); one evergreen tree (minimum 6’ to 8’ in height); a minimum 30% live plant coverage, and an automatic irrigation system operational are required elements. Design Review Where can I find an application? The applications for design review can be found by visiting the link below. Design Review Applications Design Review Can I submit a Design Review Application before I have closed on my property? Applications under contract on a property in Sterling Ranch may submit an application for Design Review, but comments and approval will not be given until the property has closed. Design Review How do I pay the Design Review application fee? Application fees can be paid via check made payable to Sterling Ranch CAB, or via credit/debit card. Please contact the team at the Resident Resource Center for assistance paying via credit/debit card. Checks can be mailed or dropped off to Sterling Ranch CAB, 8220 Piney River Ave, Littleton, CO 80125. Design Review After I receive my approval, can I modify or deviate from my application slightly? Approval was granted based on the information the homeowner provided to the committee on the application. A new Design Review Application will need to be submitted should a homeowner need to make any changes to the original application. (EXCEPT for plant material selection as long as it is for water to water same) Design Review How long does the Design Review Process take? The Design Review Committee has up to 30 days to review a submittal from the date a completed submittal package was received at the Design Review Committee meeting. If you have not been notified in writing by the 31st day after the meeting, the submittal is deemed to be denied. It is the responsibility of the applicant to contact the Design Review Committee to determine the status of the submittal. Design Review How many days do I have to install my rear yard? The rear yard landscape must be completed within 120 days following your closing. A Winter Deferral Period for completion of rear yard planting is granted for closings from November 1 to April 30. Design Review Am I allowed to make changes to my grading or drainage? The DRC does not evaluate changes to grading or drainage. Applicants are to seek approval from the County and/or other appropriate governing bodies. The DRC is not responsible in any way for changes made to grading and/or drainage while installing landscaping or other improvements. All County and State code requirements are to be followed and are the sole responsibility of the homeowner. Design Review Do I need Design Review Committee approval for my fence installation? No, fences are installed on property lines and must meet the Sterling Ranch fence design specifications. A friendly reminder to always call 811 for a utilities/wire locate before ever digging for anything in your yard. Design Review Am I limited to the plants on the Pre-Approved Recommend Plant List? Sterling Ranch collaborated with Denver Botanic Gardens to research plantings that flourish in Colorado’s semi-arid climate. The concerted research effort trialed planting for water sustainability and resiliency and took form as a test garden planted on the property that was maintained and observed for three years. The recommend plant list is a great start to understanding the Sterling Ranch planting palette, but the Design Review Committee will review additional plant material requests. Design Review Am I limited to the landscape contractors on the Pre-Approved Landscaper List? No, you may work with a landscaper of your choice, but that professional landscaper will need to meet with our Architectural and Community Standards Director to become certified and approved. The approval process includes education on Sterling Ranch Water Demand Management Initiatives and the Design Review process. Please note, inclusion on this list does not constitute the CAB’s endorsement of any of these companies. This list is only intended to identify the individuals that have attended the CAB’s required informational sessions regarding the Sterling Ranch Water Demand Management Initiatives. The CAB does not independently investigate the professional qualifications or reputations of the companies on this list. It is recommended that you perform a due diligence investigation as you would with any other company you are hiring to provide services for your home.
